title: The sage who circled only Shiva
hookLine: Bhringi circles only Shiva, so Shiva becomes half the Goddess
carry: shiva and shakti can't be pulled apart
tomorrow: a teacher leaves one teaching out. why, and who gets it?
last: A FLOWER OPENS TOWARD THE CENTER.

cards: On Mount Kailash, the sage Bhringi loves Shiva, and only Shiva.
When devotees walk around the god and the Goddess together, the way Hindus walk around a shrine, Bhringi circles Shiva alone and steps around Parvati as if she weren't there.
So Parvati sits closer, until there's no gap to step through. Bhringi turns himself into a bee and squeezes between them, still circling just one.
Then, in the telling known in Shiva's temples, Shiva does something strange. He takes Parvati into himself: one body, his right half, her left. Now there's no gap at all.

teach.b: That form has a name: Ardhanarishvara, the Lord who is half woman, carved in temples across India. Tellings of Bhringi's story vary, but the point doesn't: you can't love Shiva and leave Shakti out.
The Saundarya Lahari, the hymn that's been counting the yantra, opens on exactly this.
Its first verse says Shiva, joined with Shakti, can create; without her, he can't so much as stir. Shiva is pure awareness. Shakti is power, the Goddess as the energy in everything.
In this teaching, God is not complete without the Goddess. Now look at the Sri Yantra's heart.

teach.h: TRACE ONE TRIANGLE AT THE HEART.
teach.b: Put a fingertip on one triangle and trace it: the line runs off, crosses another and another, until you can't tell where you started.

teach.h: FOUR OF SHIVA, FIVE OF SHAKTI, WOVEN.
teach.b: The hymn names them: four triangles of Shiva and five of Shakti, nine root natures of the world. They aren't drawn side by side. They're woven, so tightly you can't lift one out.

The yantra is Bhringi's lesson, drawn in lines. Many teachers see the same truth in why so many Hindus honor the divine in pairs: Shiva with Parvati, Vishnu with Lakshmi, Rama with Sita. Not a god with a wife on the side.

how: Hindus walk clockwise around a shrine (pradakshina), and many temples and homes honor Shiva together with Parvati; Ardhanarishvara, half Shiva and half Parvati, is carved in temples across India. In Sri Vidya the interlaced triangles of the Sri Yantra are meditated on as Shiva and Shakti held together.

o: a god wearing a disguise to test his devotees
a statue carved by two artists who couldn't agree
a god who is half the Goddess, so no one can split them

games.q: two who won't come apart — tap the pairs.
p: the Lord who is half woman

s: Bhringi circled Shiva and Parvati together
he circled Shiva alone, and even became a bee to slip between them.
the Saundarya Lahari's first verse says Shiva can't even stir without Shakti
joined with her, he can create.
in the Sri Yantra, Shiva's and Shakti's triangles are drawn side by side
they're woven so tightly that none can be lifted out.

games.q: a classmate says Hindus worship a male god, with his wife on the side. what does Bhringi's story answer?
o: Shiva became half Parvati so no one could split them: Shiva and Shakti are one.
the classmate is right; the Goddess is honored only as Shiva's helper.
Bhringi was right; real devotion picks one and ignores the other.
games.why: Shiva took Parvati into himself as Ardhanarishvara, and the Saundarya Lahari says without Shakti he can't even stir. two who won't come apart.

practice: Stand, if you can, and walk one slow circle, clockwise, around a chair, a lamp or a small picture, keeping it on your right, the way Hindus circle a shrine. This is pradakshina.
As you walk, say softly, Shiva, Shakti, or, if you don't pray, just hold both words in mind. Unlike Bhringi, circle the whole thing. If walking isn't possible, trace one slow circle with a finger.

wordCard.voice: The Sri Yantra, at its heart: nine triangles, four of Shiva and five of Shakti, woven so neither stands alone.

orig.note: Sanskrit Ardhanarishvara, the Lord who is half woman: Shiva and Parvati in one body.

carryVoice: Hold onto this: Shiva and Shakti can't be pulled apart. Bhringi learned it the hard way. Day sixteen thirty-three.

sources.ref: Saundarya Lahari 1: Shiva, when joined with Shakti, is able to create; otherwise he cannot even stir
Saundarya Lahari 11: four triangles of Shiva (srikantha) and five of Shakti (shiva-yuvati), nine root natures (mula-prakriti)
Bhringi and Ardhanarishvara: the sage who circled Shiva alone, and Shiva taking Parvati as his left half (tellings vary)
